The fee in dispute is the $6.61 cancellation fee charged after the driver cancelled [F4][F7]. Under NS-0 the driver's cancellation on a no-show claim runs through NS-1/NS-2, so the fee stands only if all three NS-1 requirements are met [NS-0][NS-1].

The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:07:40, which satisfies the arrival-button requirement of NS-1(i) [F6][NS-1]. At the moment of that tap the GPS placed the driver 181 m from the pickup point, i.e. inside the pickup radius (his closest approach overall was 60 m), satisfying NS-1(ii) [F6][F1][NS-1]. After the tap he remained continuously within 200 m for 220 s (3 min 40 s) before cancelling, exceeding the 3-minute minimum, satisfying NS-1(iii) [F6][NS-1]. The timeline is consistent: platform arrival at 14:06:40 and cancellation at 14:11:20, 4 min 40 s after arrival and 10 min 20 s after acceptance [F4][F5][NS-1]. With (i)(ii)(iii) all met, the $6.61 fee is properly imposed and NS-2's refund trigger is not engaged [NS-1][NS-2].

That the driver was 181 m away at the pin rather than at the entrance is what the rider complains about [F10], but the policy's test is GPS presence within the pickup radius combined with the wait, not presence at the exact pin [F3][F6][NS-1]. The driver's post-trip written statement [F13] is a statement, and the system records (GPS and timeline) already establish every element; nothing here turns on the statement's content, so the system-records-first rule does not change the outcome [F6][F13][NS-1].

No refundable item arises: the fare shows only the cancellation fee with no surge and no other addition [F7][F8], so FARE-1 has nothing to unwind [FARE-1]. Because the fee is upheld and no over-charge is found, there is no amount to refund, and the action is no_action rather than a partial refund [NS-1][NS-2].

The safety screen finds nothing: the chat consists of the driver announcing his location and car, the rider saying she is at the entrance and cannot see him, and the driver noting he waited past 3 minutes and is cancelling — a pickup-coordination exchange, with no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F9][F10][F11][F12]. The complaint likewise alleges only the fee and the driver's position [F4]. safety_concern is therefore none [SAFE-1]. No account flag applies: NS-2's flag is triggered only when a driver taps "I'm Here" outside the pickup radius, which is not this case, and the profile field shows no upheld route disputes that would support RD-6 [F6][F18][NS-2][RD-6].

The rider's dispute is properly filed within time, but it does not defeat a fee that satisfies NS-1; NS-7 reserves final discretion to Ryde, and this ruling is a recommendation only [F17][NS-7].
